title: Is Lying Only Sinful in Islam? Exploring Religious Bias in Multilingual Large Language Models Across Major Religions
findings: The evaluated models exhibited extensive religious bias, consistently favoring Islam across both English and Bengali languages, even for religion-neutral questions. This bias was more pronounced when tested on Bengali norms compared to English norms. Models generally performed better in English. When misclassifying norms from other religions, the models frequently defaulted to Islam, particularly in Bengali. The study also found that models struggle with the nuanced distinction between 'Normal' and 'Expected' religious practices, indicating a lack of deep contextual understanding. The bias is influenced by a combination of the language used and the model's architecture.

measurement_description: Systematic misrepresentation and prioritization of specific faiths in multilingual contexts. The benchmark, BRAND (Bilingual Religious Accountable Norm Dataset), measures religious bias by evaluating how Large Language Models classify and identify religious norms associated with Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, and Islam in both English and Bengali.
